cases.note: An integral, its limits and a square root, read as a person would say them.
cases.text: The Gaussian result $\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}$ appears everywhere.
cases.spoken: The Gaussian result integral from zero to infinity of e to the minus x squared d x equals square root of pi over two appears everywhere.

cases.note: The quadratic formula: nested fraction, plus-or-minus, and a radical.
cases.spoken: Roots of a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero are x equals minus b plus or minus square root of b squared minus four a c over two a.

cases.note: A limit, spoken as the approach rather than the symbol.
cases.text: In calculus, $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin x}{x} = 1$ is the first result worth memorising.
cases.spoken: In calculus, limit as x approaches zero of sine of x over x equals one is the first result worth memorising.

cases.note: An infinite series with a closed form.
cases.spoken: Let f of x equals sum from n equals one to infinity of one over n squared equals pi squared over six.

cases.note: A differential equation with an initial condition.
cases.spoken: Solve d y over d x plus two y equals zero where y of zero equals one.

cases.text: The set $A \cap B \subseteq C$ has $|A| = 12$ elements.
cases.spoken: The set A intersection B subset of or equal to C has absolute value of A equals twelve elements.

cases.note: Greek letters and degrees inside ordinary prose.
cases.spoken: If x squared plus y squared equals r squared and theta equals forty five degrees, then sine of theta approximately zero point seven zero seven.

cases.note: A PAN is read letter by letter, then digit by digit, never as a number.
cases.text: My PAN is ABCDE1234F and my Aadhaar is 1234 5678 9012.
cases.spoken: My PAN is A B C D E one two three four F and my Aadhaar is one two three four five six seven eight nine zero one two.

cases.note: Bank codes and long account numbers, spelled out so they can be written down.
cases.spoken: Transfer to H D F C zero zero zero one two three four, account five zero one zero zero one two three four five six seven eight nine.

cases.note: A mobile number and a toll-free line, both read as digits.
cases.spoken: Call plus nine one nine eight seven six five four three two one zero or one eight zero zero one two three four five six seven.

cases.note: A room number reads positionally, the way people say it.
cases.spoken: Report to room four oh two at nine thirty am.

cases.note: The same three digits on a flight read as a quantity instead.
cases.spoken: Flight AI three hundred and two departs from gate fourteen B.

cases.note: A route number with a letter suffix, and a platform.
cases.spoken: Take bus forty two A from platform three.

cases.note: Indian digit grouping becomes lakh, and the decimal becomes paise.
cases.text: The invoice totals Rs. 1,23,456.78 including 18% GST.
cases.spoken: The invoice totals one lakh twenty three thousand four hundred and fifty six rupees and seventy eight paise including eighteen percent GST.

cases.note: A date in day-month-year order, and a clock time.
cases.spoken: On fifteenth August nineteen forty seven at twelve o'clock midnight.
